title: Conrad Biermann's copybook of outgoing letters to Danish ministers abroad, "a large part in cipher"
correspondents: Danish German Chancery (Conrad Biermann) → Danish envoys abroad (Paris, The Hague, Stockholm, Hanover ...)
shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling, Almindelig del, "Conrad Biermanns kopibog over udgående skrivelser til danske ministre i udlandet" 1675 (Daisy heid 2130515, unit S-1418)
folio_note: 255 images online (Arkivalieronline epid 15552891; image ids from 48573952). Image 109 (pp. 104-105): French letter with long runs of a numeric nomenclator (2-3 digit numbers 10-672) mixed with letters and symbols (X, #, pi-like signs), no interlinear decipherment.
status: Daisy (new search): "En stor del af de indførte skrivelser er i chifre." Viewed one opening (image 109): ciphertext copied into the register, clear text around it, no decipherment. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Key lead: Tyske Kancelli "Chiffer" 1670-1709 (heid 2132747, "a mix of many different cipher keys"), fully scanned (epid 15553654). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Copenhagen to Just Høeg at The Hague, 2, 5 and 9 January 1675, read: 841 of 849 groups, key = the untitled sheet at image 55 of the TKUA 'Chiffer' volume 1670-1709, checked on letters to Meyercrone in Paris in the same key. The rest of the copybook not reported. Extended 27 Oct 2026 (Europe chiffrée, documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675): 37 letters read with key K55, 18 to Høeg (2 Jan-5 June 1675) and 19 to Meyercrone (16 Feb-21 June; 6,103 groups, 99.4%). Still open: the letters to Lilienkron (German, numbers 14-707 with the signs Δ θ), to Gioë and Schröder (K55 family, untested) and the letter of 2 Jan to Meyercrone (another key); see the survey in targets/biermann1675/. Merged 27 Oct 2026 (pull request #133): with the eleven Høeg letters of 2 Jan-9 Feb and the 23 March letter read in targets/biermann1675 on 26 Oct, every image-55 letter to Høeg and Meyercrone is now read there.
why: Danish foreign policy at the start of the Scanian War (Gottorp, France, Sweden, Niels Brahe's mission) in the chancery's own outgoing ciphers; clear context and probable keys online.
prior_art: partial: 37 letters to Høeg (The Hague) and Meyercrone (Paris), Jan-June 1675, read by Brice Dudout, Europe chiffrée (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675), Oct 2026; key TKUA Chiffer image 55 (K55)

title: Wallis's four undeciphered 'challenge' letters at the end of his cipher book (Brasset → Bordeaux-Neufville 1653; Buckingham; Townesend 1658; unknown, Scotland 1651)
correspondents: Henri Brasset → Antoine de Bordeaux-Neufville; George Villiers, 2nd Duke of Buckingham → unknown; Peter Townesend → unknown; unknown → unknown
shelfmark: Bodleian Library, MS. e Mus. 203 pp. 218-226; copies in MS. Eng. misc. e. 475 pp. 234-247 and 'MS. 19336' pp. 203-219 (EMLO's manifestation shelfmarks)
folio_note: Letters 50-53 of Wallis's 'Collection of letters intercepted in cipher' (1653): no. 50 Brasset → Bordeaux 4 Apr 1653 (numeric + symbol substitution), no. 51 unknown, Scotland, 16 Jan 1651, no. 52 Buckingham, undated, no. 53 Peter Townesend, Flanders, 5 May 1658 (numeric substitution). EMLO works cb69093b, 3329a9ec, 86e81b88, eef01c0b.

links.label: BL Add MS 32499 f. 1 (d'Aumont cipher, Dec 1651)

status: EMLO notes for each: 'The letter is not deciphered; however, the cipher appears to be based on the substitution of numeric values.' The auction copy of the same collection (Dominic Winter, 7 Oct 2020, lot 375) says the last four letters are 'left unsolved as exercises for aspirant cryptographers'. The other 49 letters carry Wallis's decipherment and key, so related Royalist/French keys sit in the same volume. Not on DECODE under these shelfmarks (known.py: no hit for e Musaeo 203 / Eng. misc. e. 475 / Brasset 1653; DECODE has a different Brasset record R9429, Oct 1648).
why: Wallis set these as unsolved exercises; a reading would recover a 1653 French envoy's despatch on the Anglo-Dutch war and Royalist letters, and close a 370-year-old challenge.
language: French (EMLO: 'not deciphered and is in French')
prior_art: no. 52 (Buckingham) already deciphered in print: John Davys, An Essay on the Art of Decyphering (London 1737) pp. 24-29, interlinear decipherment + key, 456/480 groups (transcribed and checked 27 Oct 2026, targets/wallis1653). Davys counts three undeciphered letters in the Bodleian copy (one French, two English = nos. 50-52); no. 53 (Townesend 1658) is in the private 2020 copy. Nos. 50, 51, 53 open as far as checked (web, cryptiana, Thurloe SP i); not digitised, blocked on Bodleian access. cryptiana's 'French cipher unsolved by Wallis' is a different 1690 item, solved by Biermann 2020.

title: Aphra Behn (Astrea) → James Halsall / Thomas Killigrew, Antwerp spy letters with undecoded numeric cipher words
correspondents: Aphra Behn (with William Scot's intelligence) → James Halsall; → Thomas Killigrew

why: Fills the few code words left in Aphra Behn's 1666 espionage letters, a much-studied episode.
prior_art: in print: Taylor Editions, Oxford 2025 (Dudout, 27 Oct 2026; not verified here)
